summary: Deterministic sampled audit slice with reproducible seed and replay harness for regulator audit
description: Issue summary: AuroraBank security team requests an auditable, reproducible sample of production audit events for a regulatory review. They require that the export be deterministically sampled using a provided seed so third-party auditors can reproduce the exact subset and re-run a replay harness to validate event integrity and redaction. Impact: customer cannot complete regulator evidence packet without deterministic sampling and replay artifacts. Environment: production account (account-id: 132-998-aurora) in us-east with standard audit retention (90 days).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer attempted to request an ad-hoc audit slice via Console -> Support -> Request evidence (selected 'sampled slice, reproducible').
2) Support initiated export job using the default random sampling flow, which does not expose a stable seed for auditor replay.
3) Customer confirmed that auditors require a seed + sample algorithm (hash-based) and a replay harness to deterministically verify that sampled events are identical when re-run.
4) Attempted to re-run job with same parameters but found no seed or manifest in delivered bundle.
expected_behavior: Support export job should include: (a) deterministic seed value, (b) explicit sampling algorithm description (hash function, namespace), (c) a replay manifest with event checksums and canonical sort order, (d) signed manifest (service signing key) so auditors can verify authenticity.
actual_behavior: Export delivered as a standard sampled bundle without seed or deterministic manifest. Bundle lacks reproducible ordering and per-event checksums; auditors cannot re-run sampling to reproduce the subset.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:17 - Priya Mehta (Support): Opened ticket after phone call with AuroraBank. Customer provided regulator's acceptance criteria; uploaded as attachment.

2026-03-12 11:02 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: export pipeline uses non-deterministic shuffling step; need to add deterministic seed and canonical sort ordering. Triage to audit-service team.
2026-03-13 14:44 - AuroraBank (contact: Maria Lopez): Confirmed regulators require SHA256-based selection with seed and per-event hex checksums. Will need signed manifest for chain-of-custody.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 12:00 - SRE: Reproduced export flow in staging. Found that the sampling module uses Math.random()-based sampler. No seed or manifest emitted.

2026-03-12 15:30 - Eng (audit-service): Reviewed code path in export pipeline. Sampling implementation in analytics/exporter/sampler.go uses rand.Seed(time.Now()). Will need deterministic fallback API surface (seed param) and inclusion of manifest with event checksums and canonical sort key (timestamp + event-id).
2026-03-13 09:00 - Security: Reviewed signing requirements. Recommendation: sign manifest with service signing key v2 (rotateable) and include public key fingerprint and KMS key id in manifest.
2026-03-13 11:20 - Product: Need to confirm UI/Console flow to accept 'seed' value and checkbox for 'deterministic export for audit'. Also confirm policy for storing seed in support case (sensitive).
resolution_notes: Plan: Implement deterministic sampling path in export API (new param: deterministic_seed) that uses HMAC-SHA256(namespace || event_id || deterministic_seed) mod 1e6 for selection threshold; output manifest.json with seed, algorithm, per-event checksum (SHA256 hex), canonical_sort_key, total_count, and signed_manifest (base64 signature).

Short-term workaround: Support will run a one-off reproducible export from a controlled staging snapshot using a documented seed and produce signed manifest via ad-hoc signing script. This will be delivered to AuroraBank's auditors with a Confluence-runbook describing replay steps.

Next steps: (1) Engineering ticket to implement deterministic_seed and signed manifest API (linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821), (2) QA to validate reproducibility by re-running sampling with same seed on snapshot, (3) Security to provide KMS signing key and policy for manifest signatures, (4) Deliver interim evidence bundle to customer by 2026-03-17.
Owner: Liam O'Connor (SRE) and Priya Mehta (Support) to coordinate delivery.
